newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan sees significant reaction to budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sees significant reaction to budget pact.

text.p: A significant drop in long-term U.S. interest rates is possible if Congress and President Clinton can arrive at a credible plan to balance the budget, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Tuesday.
However, such a plan would almost certainly need to include measures to curb the growth in entitlement spending, he said.

"I would think that if you get a credible budget projection which really altered the future projection of entitlements by changing the law today ... I think the markets would respond quite positively," Greenspan told the House Budget Committee.
Speaking about the reduction in long-term interest rates that would result, the Fed chief added, "It's hard for me to put an order of magnitude on it but clearly it could be significant."
"There's a broad element of skepticism out there," Greenspan said, in explaining why a credible, long-term budget deal could lead to a drop in interest rates.
He added that in particular, the markets do not expect the Congress and the Clinton administration to do much about the biases that affect the Consumer Price Index and bloat government spending.
"I'm not sure there's much expectation in the market that something of significance will happen in this area," the Fed chief said.
